slot.brief: Charged capacitor connected to an uncharged one; compute common potential and heat lost in the process.

stem: A 5 muF capacitor is charged to 100 V and is then connected across an uncharged 20 muF capacitor. The heat generated in the connecting wires is

verdicts.working: Initial energy = ½(5 μF)(100 V)² = 25 mJ. Charge is conserved, so the final voltage is 20 V; final energy = ½(25 μF)(20 V)² = 5 mJ. Heat generated = 25 − 5 = 20 mJ.

working:
Initial energy Ui = 1/2 * C1 * V^2 = 1/2 * 5 * 10^-6 * 100^2 = 25 mJ.
Common potential Vc = C1 * V / (C1 + C2) = (5 * 10^-6 * 100) / (25 * 10^-6) = 20 V.
Final energy Uf = 1/2 * (C1 + C2) * Vc^2 = 1/2 * 25 * 10^-6 * 20^2 = 5 mJ.
Heat lost = Ui - Uf = 25 - 5 = 20 mJ.

Independent check: Initial energy = ½(5 μF)(100 V)² = 25 mJ. Charge is conserved, so the final voltage is 20 V; final energy = ½(25 μF)(20 V)² = 5 mJ. Heat generated = 25 − 5 = 20 mJ.
solution:
Charge is conserved, so the common potential is $V_f=\dfrac{C_1V}{C_1+C_2}=\dfrac{5\times100}{25}=20\,\text{V}$.
$$Q_{\text{heat}}=\frac12 C_1V^2-\frac12(C_1+C_2)V_f^2=25-5=20\,\text{mJ}$$
